dimensions.note: No argument carries a secret; ko reads registry credentials from the container config of the user running swamp. Nothing sensitive is recorded or logged.
Every method logs what it is about to do and what it did with structured placeholders; the subprocess env is never logged.

A ko or go failure throws before any write with argv, directory and stderr. Refused before ko runs: a main-package set that is empty, bare naming with several commands, a tag with bad characters, an ldflags entry with a comma, a tarball with several platforms or several commands (ko rewrites the file per run), a tarball or layout together with the daemon (ko never writes them), and a layout path ko cannot name (lowercase only). A printed reference not among the recorded ones throws.

21 unit tests with a fake go and ko cover describe (with and without a main package), build (patterns, daemon, no registry, multi-platform index and children, every refusal, failures) and resolve; the KO_E2E test runs ko 0.19.1 against fixtures/hello pushing nowhere: two commands into an OCI layout, one into a tarball, and a resolve; the three workflows ran through swamp, including ko.local into podman and a two-platform build.

Builds are reproducible by ko (trimpath); re-running build or resolve pushes the same digests; an OCI layout is appended to across runs, a tarball is one image by rule; the temporary image-refs file is removed on every path.

No HTTP; the contract is ko 0.19.1's CLI: --image-refs is parsed by digest against the last line of stdout, and the daemon publisher's digest-as-tag form is parsed too, each checked in tests. go list -f output is parsed as import path and package name.
The only temporary file is the image-refs file, removed in finally; subprocesses are awaited with the context signal.
README, skill and fixtures use example.org and registry.example.org; the fixture module is example.org/hello with no real infrastructure named.
Every resource schema is a closed z.object; no passthrough.
Every resource and the manifests file spec declare lifetime infinite and garbageCollection 10.
Builds are evidence, not a managed resource: nothing to update or delete; apply and delete were left out on purpose, rollout belongs to the deploy tooling.
arguments (policy), module-found (local) and ko-installed (local, live) run before build and resolve; describe is read.
module, build, resolution, manifests (file) and image-<command> never collide across specs; image names derive from the command's path under the module.
No method reads stored data back.
